summary: The University of Melbourne's Graduate Research Scholarships (the Melbourne Research Scholarship and the Research Training Program Scholarship) fund international and domestic students in research master's and doctoral degrees. About 600 are awarded.
meta_description: University of Melbourne Graduate Research Scholarships: full fee offset, AUD 41,100 a year (2027), relocation grant and health cover. How to be considered.
covers: A full fee offset for up to two years for a Masters by Research, or up to four years for a doctorate.
A living allowance of AUD 41,100 a year (2027 full-time rate) for up to two years for a Masters by Research, or up to three and a half years for a doctorate.
A relocation grant of AUD 3,000 for students moving from outside Australia.
Overseas Student Health Cover (single membership) for international students on a student visa.
Limited paid sick, maternity and parenting leave.
eligibility: International and domestic students who have applied for, and meet the requirements of, a graduate research degree at the University of Melbourne.
Stipend scholarships go to the candidates ranked highest by selection panels on their academic results and research potential.
how_to_apply: Apply for a Masters by Research or doctoral degree by the closing date for that course.
You are considered automatically: no separate scholarship application is needed.
You will be told within ten business days that a scholarship application has been added to your record; offers come around the same time as course offers.
watch_out: Closing dates are set by each faculty, so check the date for your course before you plan around it.
The University of Melbourne charges no application fee for graduate research courses (coursework applicants pay AUD 154).
